learning_outcomes.text: Draft technical specifications that enable posing a mechatronic engineering problem while maintaining a global and integrating vision and using prescriptive, procedural, or performance specifications as appropriate.
Organize conceptual design activity to support decision-making and selection among possible solutions to a mechatronic engineering problem.
Document the specification, implementation, and commissioning of mechatronic equipment and systems, taking into account technical aspects and relevant regulatory standards.
Students know how to apply acquired knowledge and problem-solving skills in new or unfamiliar environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their field of study.
Students know how to communicate their conclusions and the knowledge and ultimate reasons that support them to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Students possess the learning skills that will allow them to continue studying in a largely self-directed or autonomous manner.
Plan the assembly, commissioning, and maintenance of a mechatronic equipment or system.
Incorporate the necessary electrical, hydraulic, and pneumatic sensors and actuators based on the characteristics of the mechatronic system, its specifications, and integration with it.
Select electronic devices for instrumentation and control that allow conditioning and processing analog and digital signals from sensors and sent to typical actuators of a mechatronic system.
Identify the subcomponents of a technologically complex system, the interactions between them, and the effects and consequences of their possible redesign.
Discriminate the most critical components in a mechatronic system and justify their possible redesign from the perspective of the control system.
Analyze and design basic amplification circuits with operational amplifiers as well as select the appropriate operational amplifier for a given application.
Analyze and design linear power supplies.
Understand the general principles of the most important sensor types and characteristics, and select an appropriate sensor for elementary applications.
Select, analyze, and, in some cases, design basic signal conditioning circuits.
Simulate analog electronic circuits using commonly used software tools.
Design printed circuit boards using Electronic CAD tools.

assessment_methods.method: Work 1: Familiarization with sensors and Arduino connection (individual)
Work 2: Design of printed circuit boards using Proteus software (individual)
Work 3: Design and testing of a signal conditioning circuit (group of 2)

assessment_rules: For ordinary calls, assessment is based on three assignments: Work 1 (20%), Work 2 (30%), and Work 3 (50%). For extraordinary calls, Work 2 and Work 3 are maintained, and Work 1 is replaced by a multiple-choice exam covering basic concepts learned throughout the course.
